overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation. Email allegations for Sept 12, Sept 19 and Oct 10 were untimely; the Oct 17 email and Acting Chair contacts were not deliberation; non-OML issues were declined.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged improper email deliberation by the Board on September 12, September 19, and October 10, filed with the Board about two months later.
allegations.key_passage: we find that this portion of your complaint is untimely and we decline to review it.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board deliberated by email on October 17, in an October 17 email from the Health Director to the Health Agent and complainant's attorney.
allegations.key_passage: Because this communication was between individuals who are not members of the Board, the communication did not constitute deliberation.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Acting Chair and Health Director communicated about the Bayberry Avenue appeal outside a posted meeting.
allegations.key_passage: As such, we find that the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law by deliberating outside of a properly posted meeting.

allegations.summary: Complaint raised the Board's failure to grant a hearing, its authority to enforce the state sanitary code, and failure to respond to document requests.
allegations.key_passage: any allegations raised in the complaint with respect to the Board's failure to grant a hearing, authority to enforce the state sanitary code, or failure to respond to requests for documents do not constitute violations of the Open Meeting Law and we decline to review those matters.
